{
  "rules": [
    "If sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.",
    "If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ 0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% for next period.",
    "After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overcorrects and forecasts a prolonged flat or downward trend — adjust downward by 3–8% in next 3–5 days.",
    "When sentiment is flat (all 0.00), model often fails to capture mean reversion; apply a 1–3% upward bias to forecast if recent price is below 30-day moving average.",
    "If model forecast is rising steadily with no sentiment signal, it may be overconfident; cap forecast increase at 1% per day unless sentiment confirms bullish momentum.",
    "In cases where true outcome shows strong downward correction after a peak, model often fails to recognize the lag — delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and reduce slope of decline.",
    "If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.00, 0.67), model may misread momentum — use sentiment-weighted average to smooth forecast curve."
  ]
}
